page: Hetzner Cloud cpx42 is an x86_64 virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC processor running under the QEMU hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with 320 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, though the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the cpx42 demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring in the top 25% for both stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core metrics. Large-block memory bandwidth is also a notable strength, with read-only and write speeds reaching 255.54 GB/sec and 168.09 GB/sec respectively. Multi-core performance, including Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core tests, falls within the average range. The server also delivers average throughput for tasks such as static web serving, Redis SET operations, and database operations.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the cpx42 is its shared CPU allocation, which can introduce performance variability under sustained multi-core loads compared to dedicated thread alternatives. However, this shared model delivers high qualitative cost efficiency, offering a substantial 320 GB NVMe storage allocation and 8 vCPUs at a budget-friendly resource density. This configuration is well-suited for workloads such as single-threaded applications, lightweight web serving, development environments, and moderate database operations that benefit from fast local storage and strong single-core burst capabilities.
